name: Job posting and sourcing plan
summary: For one approved role, the hiring manager gets a plan for where to post and where to look: every channel on the company's own list ordered by the signal it should give for that kind of role, a week-by-week schedule inside the budget, and what to count on each channel. Nothing is posted or paid until a person approves.

sources.title: The channel types, the starting table by role family, the rule that the company's own counts replace it, the choosing rules for budget, hours and a weekly cap, the weekly schedule, the measurement and review rules, the check that at least one channel is open to anyone, the stop conditions, the tests and the worked example.

sources.contribution: Choosing channels by the kind of role and ordering them by useful response for their cost; a few well-chosen channels in place of every board; looking for people through networks, investors and communities as well as by posting; counting applicant quality by channel to adjust the mix; and posting to diversity-focused channels, the root of the template's check for channels that reach groups the company wants more applicants from.
